docs.title: Quota Dashboard Runbook
docs.text:
How to deploy, look after and fix the Quota Dashboard (the quoting tool for Jordan Select Tours and Jordan Direct Tours). Written for whoever is on duty, including when the usual person is away. Every page is a short list of steps.

Something is broken right now?

Go straight to The site is down: first five minutes.

docs.title: Pick what you need
docs.text: I want to... Go to Open a terminal on the server Connect with SSH Install it on a new machine First install Put a new version live Update to a new version Undo a bad version Go back Check it is healthy Daily health check Back up or copy backups Backups Change a password or key Passwords and keys Bring the data back Restore the database Fix a PDF, email or picture error Common errors

docs.title: What it is made of
docs.text:
Box What it does frontend The website staff open (nginx). It also passes requests to the backend. backend The brain: prices quotes, builds offers and PDFs, sends email, hands booked quotes to the CRM. db The database (PostgreSQL). All quotes and the catalogue live here. backup A helper that saves a copy of the database every night.

All run together with Docker Compose. A volume is the folder Docker keeps data in, so data survives restarts. The ones that matter: pgdata (the database) and backups (the nightly copies). The pictures offers show are in a separate folder on the server (MEDIA_ROOT), not in the database.

docs.title: Unlike the CRM, nothing deploys by itself
docs.text: When code is pushed to GitHub, robots only test it. They do not update the server. Someone must log in and run the update steps. That also means the database update is a separate step you must run yourself.

docs.title: The golden rules
docs.text:
1. Back up before any update. See Backups.
  2. Never delete a Docker volume. Never run docker compose down -v or docker volume prune.
  3. After every update, run the database update step, or pages will error.
  4. Read the error before you act. Start at the site-down page.
  5. Write down what you did, with times.

docs.title: Who to contact
docs.text:
(Name, phone, role. Fill this in.)

Keep this site free of secrets

GitHub Pages sites are public. Never write passwords, keys, IP addresses or customer data here.

docs.title: Connect to the server (SSH)
docs.text:
When to use this: Any page that says "open a terminal on the server". Time it takes: 5 minutes (first time: 15) You need: The server address and your username from the person who manages access, and to be on the office network (or VPN).

SSH lets you type commands on the server from your own computer, securely.

The address and username are not on this site

This site is public. Ask the developer, or look in the team password manager. Replace <username>, <server-address> and <quota-folder> below.

docs.title: Steps: the first time
docs.text:
1. Open a terminal (Mac: Terminal. Windows: PowerShell). SSH is already installed.
  2. Create your own key (skip if you have one). Choose a passphrase and remember it.
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "your-name-laptop"
  1. Show your public key and send the whole line to the person managing the server:
cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub

!!! danger "Never share the private key" The file without .pub stays on your computer. Never send it or paste it anywhere.

  1. After they add it, connect:
ssh <username>@<server-address>
  1. The first time it asks Are you sure you want to continue connecting (yes/no)? Type yes.
  2. Go to the Quota folder (the one that contains the deploy and backend folders):
cd <quota-folder>
ls

You should see backend, frontend and deploy. Run every command on this site from this folder.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
hostname
docker compose version

The first shows the server's name, not your computer's.

docs.title: Leaving
docs.text: exit

docs.title: Safety
docs.text:
• Use only your own key. Do not run commands you do not understand.
  • Never run docker compose down -v or docker volume prune.
  • If your laptop is lost, tell the server manager at once so your key is removed.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
You see Do this Connection timed out Not on the office network or VPN, or the server is off. Connection refused Server on, SSH not running, or wrong address. Ask the developer. Permission denied (publickey) Your key was not added, or wrong username. REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED Stop and ask the developer.

Last checked: YYYY-MM-DD

docs.title: Common errors: PDF, email and pictures
docs.text:
When to use this: The site works, but one feature fails. Time it takes: 10 minutes You need: SSH access, in the Quota folder.

You see Meaning Do this 503 pdf_unavailable when opening a PDF The backend lacks a library for PDFs Rebuild without the cache: docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env build --no-cache backend then docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env up -d. Test: docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env exec backend python -c "import weasyprint" 503 mail_unavailable when sending an offer The email settings are wrong Check the SMTP_* values in deploy/.env, then docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env up -d 503 media_unavailable on a picture upload The pictures folder is missing or not writable Check MEDIA_ROOT in deploy/.env points at a real folder the server can write to Offers show no pictures The pictures folder is empty or wrong Same check as above "locked" at sign-in Five wrong attempts Wait 15 minutes, or an administrator resets the password in Administration → Users

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text: Repeat what failed: open the PDF, send a test offer, upload a picture.

docs.title: If it is still wrong
docs.text:
Copy the last 50 lines of docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env logs --tail=50 backend and send them to the developer.

Last checked: YYYY-MM-DD

docs.title: Restore the database from a backup
docs.text:
When to use this: Data was lost or damaged, or you are rebuilding a server. Time it takes: 20 minutes You need: SSH access, in the Quota folder, and a backup file ending in .sql.gz. See Backups.

This replaces everything in the live database

Anything entered after the backup was taken is lost. Tell staff to stop first. If the database still starts, take a fresh backup before you begin.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• [ ] Staff told to stop using the app.
  • [ ] You know which backup file and its date.
  • [ ] The file is on the server. To take one from the backup volume:
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env cp backup:/backups ./backups-copy
ls backups-copy

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Stop everything that uses the database:
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env stop backend backup
  1. Empty the database:
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env exec -T db psql -U postgres -c 'DROP DATABASE quota' -c 'CREATE DATABASE quota'
  1. Load the backup (change the file name):
gunzip -c backups-copy/quota_<date>.sql.gz | docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env exec -T db psql -U postgres quota
  1. Start everything and bring the database shape up to date:
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env start backend backup
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env exec backend alembic upgrade head

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
• docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env ps shows all boxes running.
  • Sign in and open a recent quote and its offer.
  • Tell staff which date and time the data goes back to, so they can re-enter anything missing.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
You see Do this database "quota" is being accessed by other users Step 1 did not stop everything. Run it again and check with docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env ps. gzip: not in gzip format Wrong or damaged file. Try another backup. service "db" is not running docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env up -d db, wait a minute, retry from step 2. Errors about missing columns after the restore Run docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env exec backend alembic upgrade head again.

Last checked: YYYY-MM-DD

docs.title: The server is gone
docs.text:
When to use this: The machine died, was stolen, or its disk is destroyed. Time it takes: About an hour, plus downloads You need: GitHub access to both repositories, a new Linux machine with Docker, the settings file (deploy/.env) from the team password manager, the newest backup copy stored off the server, and the pictures folder.

This is why copies must be kept off the server

If every backup was on the dead machine, the data may be gone. Check laptops, cloud drives, and colleagues first.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Prepare a new machine with Linux, Docker and the compose plugin.
  2. Install it by following First install steps 1 to 3. Use the saved deploy/.env instead of writing a new one. If you must make a new one, the password must match whatever the restored database expects (ask the developer).
  3. Put the pictures folder back and point MEDIA_ROOT at it.
  4. Restore the data with Restore the database, using your newest backup.
  5. Tell staff the new address if it changed, and update PUBLIC_BASE_URL if so.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
• You can sign in, open a recent quote, and view an offer with pictures.
  • A fresh backup exists and is copied off the machine.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
You see Do this No backup can be found Check every device and cloud account the team uses. Tell the developer immediately. The newest backup is old Restore it anyway, then have staff re-enter newer work.

Last checked: YYYY-MM-DD

docs.title: The site is down: first five minutes
docs.text:
When to use this: Staff cannot open the Quota Dashboard, or every page shows errors. Time it takes: 5 minutes to find the cause You need: SSH access, in the Quota folder.

Stay calm, change one thing at a time

Your data is safe in the database volume. Most problems are fixed by a restart. Do not delete anything.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. What is running?
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env ps

Any box that is exited, restarting or unhealthy is the suspect.

  1. Is the computer OK?
df -h

100% full stops the database. Tell the developer; do not delete volumes.

  1. Read the last messages:
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env logs --tail=100 backend
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env logs --tail=50 db

  1. Match what you see with the table below.

  2. If unsure, restart. It keeps all data.

docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env restart

If that does not help:

docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env down
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env up -d

Never add -v to down: it erases the database.

docs.title: What you see and what to do
docs.text: You see Meaning Do this Site will not load, frontend not running The web box stopped docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env up -d Page loads, actions give 502 The web box cannot reach the backend docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env restart backend frontend backend keeps restarting Often the database is down, or a setting is wrong Read the backend logs; check db db not running Database stopped Check disk (step 2), then up -d. If it will not start: Restore Errors about a missing column or table New code, old database shape Run docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env exec backend alembic upgrade head "locked" at sign-in Too many wrong passwords Wait 15 minutes A PDF, email or picture error A single feature, not the whole site Common errors Whole server does not answer Off or network down The server is gone Just updated New version problem Go back

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
curl http://localhost/health
curl http://localhost/api/v1/health/db

Then sign in and open a quote.

docs.title: After it is fixed
docs.text:
• Write down what happened, what you did, and the times.
  • Tell the team it is back.
  • Take a fresh backup.

Last checked: YYYY-MM-DD

docs.title: What happens when code is pushed (CI)
docs.text: When to use this: You want to know what the green or red tick on GitHub means. Time it takes: 3 minutes to read

docs.title: The short version
docs.text:
Every push to the main branch and every pull request starts a robot called CI on GitHub. It:

  1. starts a temporary database,
  2. checks the code style,
  3. runs the automatic tests.

That is all it does. It does not update the server. A green tick means "the code passed its tests", not "it is live".

docs.title: To put a new version live
docs.text: Follow Update to a new version.

docs.title: Reading the result
docs.text:
Open the repository on GitHub → Actions tab.

You see Meaning Green tick Tests passed. Safe to update. Red cross A test or style check failed. Do not update. Tell the developer. Yellow dot Still running. Wait.

Last checked: YYYY-MM-DD

docs.title: First install
docs.text: When to use this: Setting up Quota Dashboard on a new machine. Time it takes: 45 minutes You need: A Linux machine with Docker and the compose plugin (about 2 GB of disk), SSH access, GitHub access to both repositories, and the legacy images/ folder somewhere on the machine.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• [ ] Decide the web address staff will use.
  • [ ] Have these values ready (never write them on this site): a database password, a signing key (long random text), mail (SMTP) settings, and the path to the pictures folder.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Get both repositories. The front end goes inside the backend's folder.
git clone git@github.com:AbuEnzo/quota-dashboard-backend.git quota
git clone git@github.com:AbuEnzo/quota-dashboard-frontend.git quota/frontend
cd quota
  1. Create the settings file and fill it in.
cp deploy/.env.example deploy/.env
nano deploy/.env

Set PUBLIC_BASE_URL, MEDIA_ROOT (the pictures folder), POSTGRES_PASSWORD, JWT_SECRET and the SMTP_* values. Save with Ctrl+O, Enter, Ctrl+X.

  1. Build and start.
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env up -d --build
  1. Create the database tables.
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env exec backend alembic upgrade head
  1. Load the catalogue from the old system (it must be reachable from the server):
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env exec backend python scripts/import_legacy.py
  1. Create the first administrator. Choose a strong password in place of choose-one.
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env exec -e SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD='choose-one' backend python scripts/seed_admin.py admin@example.com "Administrator"
  1. Add https. Put the office's TLS proxy (Caddy, Traefik, or the existing nginx) in front of the web port, and set PUBLIC_BASE_URL to the https address. Then COOKIE_SECURE=true applies. Run step 3 again after changing the settings.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
curl http://localhost/health
curl http://localhost/api/v1/health/db

The first answers {"status":"ok"}. The second shows the database and its version. Then open the address in a browser and sign in as the administrator.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
You see Do this set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in deploy/.env The settings file is missing a value. Edit deploy/.env. set MEDIA_ROOT in deploy/.env Point it at the pictures folder. Import cannot reach the legacy database The old database address is wrong or not reachable from the container. Ask the developer. Anything else Site is down

Last checked: YYYY-MM-DD

docs.title: Go back to the last working version
docs.text:
When to use this: A new version broke something and you need the old one. Time it takes: 15 minutes You need: SSH access and the version codes you wrote down before the update.

Going back does not undo database changes

The database update (step 3 of Update) only moves forward. If the new version changed the database and the old code cannot work with it, restore the backup taken before the update.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• [ ] Take a backup of the current state.
  • [ ] Have the two old version codes (backend and frontend).

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. In the Quota folder, check out the old versions:
git checkout <old-backend-code>
git -C frontend checkout <old-frontend-code>
  1. Rebuild and restart:
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env up -d --build

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
• docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env ps shows all boxes running.
  • Sign in and open a quote.

Remember to return to the latest later

The server is now parked on an old version. When the fix is ready, run git checkout main && git pull (and the same with git -C frontend) before following Update, or future updates will not work.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
You see Do this Errors about missing columns The database is ahead of the code. Restore the backup. error: pathspec ... did not match The version code is wrong. Check it with git log --oneline.

Last checked: YYYY-MM-DD

docs.title: Update to a new version
docs.text:
When to use this: The developers pushed new code and you want it live. Time it takes: 10 minutes You need: SSH access. Nothing updates automatically, so someone has to do this.

Staff may see a short pause

The site restarts. Do it outside office hours when you can.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• [ ] Be in the Quota folder on the server.
  • [ ] Take a backup.
  • [ ] Check GitHub: the latest push on main should have a green tick (its tests passed).
  • [ ] Write down the version you are on, so you can go back:
git rev-parse --short HEAD
git -C frontend rev-parse --short HEAD

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Download the new code for both repositories:
git pull
git -C frontend pull
  1. Rebuild and restart:
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env up -d --build
  1. Update the database. This is not automatic. Skipping it causes errors.
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env exec backend alembic upgrade head

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env ps
curl http://localhost/health
  • db, backend, frontend and backup are running.
  • Open the site, sign in, open a quote, and open its offer.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
You see Do this git pull says local changes would be overwritten Someone edited files on the server. Do not force it; ask the developer. Pages show errors about a missing column or table Step 3 was not run, or failed. Run it and read the message. The database update step fails Go back, then tell the developer the error. Site is down after the update Site is down

Last checked: YYYY-MM-DD

docs.title: Backups
docs.text: When to use this: Before every update, and to make sure copies exist off the server. Time it takes: 5 minutes You need: SSH access, in the Quota folder.

docs.title: What is already automatic
docs.text:
A helper box called backup saves a copy of the database every night (at the hour set in the settings, 02:00 by default), plus once each time it starts. Copies are kept 30 days by default and older ones are deleted. They live in the backups volume, on the same server as the database.

A copy on the same machine is not enough

If the server dies, those copies die with it. Copy them elsewhere regularly.

docs.title: Copy the nightly backups off the server
docs.text:
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env cp backup:/backups ./backups-copy

Then move the backups-copy folder to another computer or a cloud drive.

docs.title: Take a backup by hand (before an update)
docs.text:
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env exec -T db pg_dump -U postgres quota | gzip > quota_manual.sql.gz

Use a clear name if you keep several, for example quota_before-update-2026-11-01.sql.gz.

docs.title: The pictures are not in the database
docs.text: The pictures offers show are in the MEDIA_ROOT folder on the server. Back that folder up with the server's normal file backups. The generated PDFs are only a cache and are made again when needed.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
• The file exists and is not tiny: ls -lh quota_manual.sql.gz.
  • A backup you have never restored is a hope. Once, on a spare machine, try Restore the database.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
You see Do this service "db" is not running The database is stopped: Site is down An empty or very small file The command failed; check the disk with df -h and retry "pg_dump failed" in the backup log Check the disk and the database password in the settings

Last checked: YYYY-MM-DD

docs.title: Daily health check
docs.text: When to use this: Every morning, or whenever you want to be sure it is OK. Time it takes: 3 minutes You need: A browser; for the full check, SSH access.

docs.title: Quick check
docs.text:
1. Open the Quota Dashboard and sign in.
  2. Open a recent quote and its offer.
  3. Open http://<server>/health in a browser. It should answer {"status":"ok"}.

docs.title: Full check (on the server, in the Quota folder)
docs.text:
1. See every box:
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env ps

Good looks like: db, backend, frontend and backup all running.

  1. Check the database answers:
curl http://localhost/api/v1/health/db
  1. Look at the latest backend messages:
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env logs --tail=50 backend
  1. Check the last backup was made:
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env logs --tail=5 backup

You should see a line like backup: wrote /backups/quota_<date>.sql.gz.

  1. Check disk space (a full disk stops the database):
df -h

Worry above about 85% used.

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
You see Do this A box is restarting or exited Site is down No recent backup line, or "pg_dump failed" Check the disk, then take a manual backup Disk above 85% Tell the developer. Never delete Docker volumes.

Last checked: YYYY-MM-DD

docs.title: Passwords and keys
docs.text: When to use this: A password was shared by mistake, someone left, or a user is locked out. Time it takes: 10 minutes You need: SSH access, in the Quota folder; or an administrator login.

docs.title: A user is locked out
docs.text: Five wrong sign-in attempts in fifteen minutes lock the account for fifteen minutes. Wait fifteen minutes, or an administrator can reset the password in the app: Administration → Users.

docs.title: Sign everyone out and replace the signing key
docs.text:
The signing key (JWT_SECRET) proves a sign-in is genuine. Changing it signs everyone out.

  1. Edit the settings file:
nano deploy/.env
  1. Replace the JWT_SECRET value with a new long random text. Save (Ctrl+O, Enter, Ctrl+X).
  2. Restart:
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml --env-file deploy/.env up -d

docs.title: Change the database password
docs.text: Do not do this alone: the password is stored in two places (the database and the settings file). Ask the developer.

docs.title: The settings file
docs.text: deploy/.env holds every secret. It is never in git. Keep a copy in the team password manager, because if the server is lost the file is lost too.

docs.title: Check it worked
docs.text:
• After a key change, you are asked to sign in again.
  • A new password lets the user in.

Last checked: YYYY-MM-DD
